learn.why: On stream I do not want chat watching me read a wall of underlined words. C keeps the crisis text clean and dramatic, and the full-screen 'What is going on here?' drawer with map, who is who and 'what really happened' is a visual moment I can open on camera and talk over. The '+4 new in your codex' toast is a small hit of progression. A is okay, the hover popup with the little map is nice, but it covers the choice cards. B is a boring sidebar list.
would_turn_off: underlines (look like links, clutter on camera)
the 'i' per paragraph if it gets noisy on screen
Brief me on each new crisis (auto-popup would kill the pacing)
unknown_terms_i_saw: the midterms (I know the word, not the date)

answers.Q1: Zelensky, Putin, Trump, Macron, Moscow, Washington I know. Donetsk oblast, fortress belt, Kramatorsk, Sloviansk, the Rada, Pokrovsk, Oleshky, Dnipro I could not explain to a friend. Fortress belt: look up now because it sounds like a boss level. The rest: later or never.
answers.Q2: A: maybe, soft underlines are fine but the popup covered the cards, and underlines look like ad links on stream. B: no, a sidebar list means I look away from the drama. C: yes, text stays clean and the big drawer is a thing I can open on purpose.
answers.Q3: Fortress belt, variant A or C. A: hover shows it at once, clear in one read, 5. C: the drawer is clear but I have to click, 4.
answers.Q5: Some help. Turn off underlines first, then the toast if it covers the choice cards.
answers.Q6: Yes, I would open it once per new crisis, for the content, not to choose. First read: the map, then who is who. The one-line summary is fine as a caption. Missing: what each choice would do to the war, honestly I would pick by the cards anyway.
answers.Q7: 18 of 31 met is a collect-them-all bar, that I like, mild pull. I would glance at the codex after the game ends only if it makes a shareable card.
answers.Q8: A 15, B 5, C1 5, C2 30, D 15, E 10, F 20 (sum 100). Note F and C2 are high because I want to skip help fast and open the big view for content.
answers.Q9: C, and make the drawer a full-screen cinematic stinger with a short fade-in so it looks great on stream.
answers.Q10: Do not care about 'As of Nov 2026' or the source count. One wrong fact would not stop me, I would make it a joke, unless it is wrong about something chat knows. Facts flagged: none.

worldmap.why: A looks like a war room: every situation has a name label on the globe, I can read the story at a glance and it is better on camera. B is prettier in the colours but the numbered fires make me read a side list. Chat will want to point at names on the map. Better with B's rim markers and bigger names.
unknown_terms_i_saw: Divided Berlin (I know the idea, not the 1960 story)

answers.Q1: S1 (A): 1960 from the title and the Soviet Union, a Cold War split, Berlin, a nuke thing in Africa and a war in Algeria. S4 (B): also 1960, but I had to look at the right panel. A told me faster.
answers.Q2: Yes, different worlds: Soviet Union and Warsaw Pact red in 1960 and in 2026 Russia and a different set of pins (S1 vs S2). Nothing looked wrong to me, but I would not know a Belgian Congo error anyway.
answers.Q3: Names readable on desktop. In S1 the Laos and Vietnam pin label sits over Iran and Pakistan region and Iraq/Iran labels crowd each other. In S2 the Hormuz card covers Iran and Gulf names. Missing: Japan, Mexico, Brazil, Germany label on 1960 (West Germany is there).
answers.Q4: The Taiwan Strait shelling anchor pin: I guess a naval standoff. Hollow dashed brewing pins versus solid ones read OK. Dotted rival lines versus solid red war front read fine, the red arc in S2 is cool.
answers.Q5: I noticed 3, 4, 5 in S4 only because of the numbers on the rim. I would expect a tap to spin the globe to it, that would be a nice show.
answers.Q6: Card next to the pin (S2) is faster for me, I do not look away. The panel (S4) shows more but is more reading. Phone view not my device.
answers.Q7: Leave A's all-on default, it fills the screen with stuff to talk about. I would flip B's switch immediately.
answers.Q8: Blocs (A) helped me pick a nation, colours obvious: blue NATO, red Warsaw Pact. B's stability glow is pretty, but orange versus red-brown is hard to tell apart.
answers.Q9: Worth having, it is a clip moment: the year rolling and sepia 1960 settling. I would flip eras more just to show chat. Sound on the year stamp would be a bonus.
answers.Q10: Yes, both fill the screen far better than the S0 title globe. Phone not tested.
answers.Q11: A, with B's rim markers and spin-to-pin. One change: make the pins pulse and the labels bigger so it is readable at stream size.

verbatim: Give me the big full-screen briefing and the war-room map with names on every fire, keep the little underlines off my stream, and let me flip eras with a sound so chat can clip it.
